presets.title: Build a looping campfire with flames, embers and smoke
presets.summary: A new Niagara System with three named, live emitters in warm colours, placed in the level and captured over time.
presets.prompt:
Build a looping campfire `{{content_folder}}/{{system_name}}` with exactly three emitters: `Flames` (orange to yellow, rising), `Embers` (small bright sparks drifting up) and `Smoke` (soft grey, slow, gone within 4 s). Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall `vfx fire` for project conventions. hyper_niagara_discover with kind recipe, recipe fire and targetPath the new System: it returns the ops for Flames and Embers (part 2 adds Smoke) and the particle materials they use. Make each missing material with hyper_material_recipe as its line says.
2. hyper_niagara_apply_plan with recipe fire, recipeSettings ["scale=1"], the new targetPath, an empty expectedRevision, bDryRun false and a fresh operationId. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId. Then hyper_niagara_inspect for the new revision and the same call with recipeSettings ["part=2"] and that expectedRevision, which adds Smoke.
3. hyper_niagara_preview of the System with ages [0.5, 1, 2]; open the image and check the flames read orange to yellow and rise, embers drift up and smoke is soft and grey (background grey for the smoke). Tune with one more plan (hyper_niagara_inspect first for the revision) if they do not.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then policy runtime_probe with expectEmitters [Flames, Embers, Smoke] and minParticlesPerEmitter 5.
5. Place it in {{level}} at {{location}} as an actor labelled `Campfire` with Epic's add_to_scene_from_asset; leave the level unsaved. hyper_capture_view with source transform, 500 cm from the fire and looking at it, frameCount 3, intervalSeconds 0.25.
6. Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: runtime_ready with 0 errors and 0 warnings; each emitter live with its particle count; changedPixelFraction between frames above 0.01; the flames read orange to yellow in the frames. Show each frame on its own line as ![frame](path).

presets.title: Add a sparkle and glow loop to a pickup
presets.summary: A small looping effect with a soft glow, a point light and twinkling sparkles, placed on the selected pickup and kept under a particle budget.
presets.prompt:
Give the pickup {{selected_actor}} a looping sparkle effect `{{content_folder}}/{{system_name}}`: a soft `Glow` sprite with a point light and `Sparkles` twinkling around it, tinted {{color}}, never more than {{max_particles}} particles. Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_scene_inspect with scope selected for the pickup's location. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): add_emitter `Glow` from SingleLoopingParticle and `Sparkles` from HangingParticulates (both in /Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters); add_renderer /Script/Niagara.NiagaraLightRendererProperties on Glow; set_emitter_property `enabled` false on each template emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Inspect again (new revision, modules, inputs, renderer indexes), then one plan (up to 96 ops): set_input_value for colour, size, spawn rate and a Sparkles spawn shape about 60 cm across; set_renderer_property RadiusScale on Glow's light renderer (its rendererIndex from inspect).
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [Glow, Sparkles].
5. Place it at the pickup's location with Epic's add_to_scene_from_asset, labelled `{{system_name}}_FX`; leave the level unsaved. hyper_capture_view with source transform, 300 cm away and looking at it, frameCount 2, intervalSeconds 0.5.
6. Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: both emitters live, total live particles at most {{max_particles}}, a light renderer on Glow, 0 errors and 0 warnings. Show each frame on its own line as ![frame](path).

presets.title: Audit a Niagara System's health without changing it
presets.summary: Topology, compile state, stack issues with fix ids and live particle counts for the selected System, checked against the effects quality bar.
presets.prompt:
Audit the Niagara System {{selected_asset}} and change nothing. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall `vfx budget` with target {{selected_asset}} for known issues and the project's VFX budgets.
2. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true (load it with Epic's load_asset if it answers target_not_loaded): list each emitter with its sim target, renderers, simulation stages and scratch pad modules, the user parameters and the effect type.
3. hyper_niagara_validate with policy authoring, then runtime_ready: every issue with its severity and fixIds.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_probe and probeFrames 120: each emitter's live and spawned counts and their count source (cpu or gpu_estimate).
5. Flag what breaks the effects bar: any compile error or warning; an enabled emitter that is not live; more than {{max_particles}} live particles in one emitter; a GPU emitter without fixed bounds (Epic's GetEmitterData shows its bounds mode); no effect type.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table, one row per check and emitter with the numbers, then the fixes you recommend, each named by the plan op kind that would make it (apply_stack_issue_fix, set_emitter_property, set_input_value, set_effect_type). Apply nothing.

presets.title: Repair a broken Niagara System's compile and stack issues
presets.summary: Apply the stack's own fixes and replace failing HLSL modules in reviewed plans until the System compiles clean and every emitter spawns.
presets.prompt:
Repair the Niagara System {{selected_asset}} so it compiles clean and every enabled emitter spawns. Change only this System; each plan compiles and saves it. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true and keep the revision. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready: list every issue with its issueId and fixIds.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan, first with bDryRun true because it may touch many modules, then the same ops with bDryRun false, a fresh operationId and expectedRevision: an apply_stack_issue_fix op per fixable issue; for an HLSL module that fails to compile, set_module_enabled false on it and add_hlsl_module with a corrected copy under a new name. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Inspect again for the new revision and repeat step 2, at most {{max_rounds}} rounds, while fixable issues remain.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with minParticlesPerEmitter 1.
5. hyper_log_tail with contains `Niagara` for compile errors the stack did not report.
Reply with a before/after PASS/FAIL table: error and warning counts, each issue fixed or left (and why), each enabled emitter live. Name any link-style issue that needs the Niagara editor, and any disabled module Epic's RemoveModule could now delete.

presets.title: Make GPU snowfall over an area with fixed bounds
presets.summary: A GPU snow emitter spawning over a sized box with wind and curl-noise drift, explicit bounds, a bounded count and captured frames.
presets.prompt:
Make GPU snowfall `{{content_folder}}/NS_Snowfall` over a {{area}} x {{area}} cm area, falling from {{height}} cm to the ground. Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall `weather vfx`. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): add_emitter `Snow` from /Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/HangingParticulates.HangingParticulates (WindForce included); add_module /Niagara/Modules/Spawn/Location/BoxLocation.BoxLocation in its ParticleSpawnScript and /Niagara/Modules/Update/Forces/CurlNoiseForce.CurlNoiseForce in its ParticleUpdateScript; set_emitter_property sim_target gpu and fixed_bounds over the area from 0 to {{height}} cm; set_emitter_property `enabled` false on each template emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Inspect again (new revision, modules, inputs, renderer indexes), then one plan (up to 96 ops): set_module_enabled false on Snow's ShapeLocation; set_input_value for a box of the whole area at {{height}} cm, about {{spawn_rate}} per second, a WindForce velocity carrying flakes down at 100-200 cm/s with slight drift, gentle curl noise, and a lifetime that reaches the ground.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [Snow].
5. Place it at the origin of {{level}} (unsaved) and hyper_capture_view, source transform 1500 cm away at eye height, frameCount 2, intervalSeconds 1.
6. Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: Snow on GPU with fixed bounds, live count at most {{spawn_rate}} x lifetime, 0 errors and 0 warnings, frames differ. Show each frame on its own line as ![frame](path).

presets.title: Build a one-shot rifle muzzle flash with sparks and light
presets.summary: A burst effect along +X: a bright flash, velocity-aligned sparks and a light, proven alive at frame 3 and gone within a second.
presets.prompt:
Build a rifle muzzle flash `{{content_folder}}/{{system_name}}` that fires once per activation along +X: `Flash` (one bright sprite, about 0.1 s), `Sparks` (15-30 velocity-aligned sparks, under 0.3 s) and a light flash tinted {{flash_color}}. Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): add_emitter `Flash` from SimpleSpriteBurst and `Sparks` from DirectionalBurst (/Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters); set_renderer_property Alignment VelocityAligned on Sparks' sprite renderer (rendererIndex 0); add_renderer /Script/Niagara.NiagaraLightRendererProperties on Flash; set_emitter_property `enabled` false on each template emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Inspect again (new revision, modules, inputs, renderer indexes), then one plan (up to 96 ops): set_input_value for burst counts, lifetimes, velocity along +X, colour {{flash_color}} and size; set_renderer_property RadiusScale on Flash's light renderer.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready.
5. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_probe, probeFrames 3 and expectEmitters [Flash, Sparks]: the burst caught alive at 0.05 s.
6. runtime_probe again with probeFrames 60. It reports not_live by design: every emitter must show 0 particles after 1 s.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: both emitters live at frame 3; Sparks totalSpawned 15-30; zero particles alive at 1 s; a light renderer on Flash; 0 errors and 0 warnings.

presets.title: Swirl an arcane portal with a custom HLSL vortex module
presets.summary: Particles spawned on a torus that spiral inward through a scratch pad HLSL module, compiled, proven live and captured in motion.
presets.prompt:
Build a swirling arcane portal `{{content_folder}}/{{system_name}}`: particles born on a ring of {{radius}} cm in the YZ plane that spiral inward around the X axis, tinted {{color}}. Follow the unreal-niagara skill and its HLSL rules; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall `vfx magic`. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): add_emitter `Swirl` from /Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/Fountain.Fountain; add_module /Niagara/Modules/Spawn/Location/TorusLocation.TorusLocation in its ParticleSpawnScript; add_hlsl_module `PortalVortex` in ParticleUpdateScript that adds a tangential velocity around X and a pull toward the axis, using only Particles.Position, Particles.Velocity and Engine.DeltaTime; set_renderer_property Alignment VelocityAligned (rendererIndex 0); set_emitter_property `enabled` false on each template emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Inspect again (new revision, modules, inputs, renderer indexes), then one plan (up to 96 ops): set_module_enabled false on Swirl's ShapeLocation and AddVelocity; set_input_value for torus radius {{radius}}, its axis along X, gravity 0, colour {{color}}.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy authoring (the HLSL compiles), runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [Swirl] and minParticlesPerEmitter 50. Inspect: PortalVortex is last in Particle Update and in scratchPadModules.
5. Place it in {{level}} (unsaved) and hyper_capture_view, source transform 600 cm along -X looking at it, frameCount 3, intervalSeconds 0.25.
6. Reply with a PASS/FAIL table of those checks. Show each frame on its own line as ![frame](path).

presets.title: Keep GPU particles above the ground with a simulation stage
presets.summary: Switch one emitter to GPU with fixed bounds, add a simulation stage and an HLSL clamp module, and prove it compiles and stays live.
presets.prompt:
In the Niagara System {{selected_asset}}, keep the `{{emitter}}` emitter's particles above z = {{ground_z}} cm with a GPU simulation stage. Change only this emitter; each plan compiles and saves the System. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true: confirm `{{emitter}}` exists and note its sim target and stages; keep the revision. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_probe and expectEmitters [{{emitter}}] as the baseline count.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision), in this order: set_emitter_property sim_target gpu; set_emitter_property fixed_bounds {{bounds}}; add_simulation_stage `Settle` with value {{iterations}}; add_hlsl_module `KeepAboveGround` with stageName Settle that clamps Particles.Position.z to at least {{ground_z}} and reflects Particles.Velocity.z at half speed. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. hyper_niagara_inspect: SimTarget GPUComputeSim, simulationStages lists Settle with {{iterations}} iterations and KeepAboveGround.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy authoring, runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [{{emitter}}] (a gpu_estimate count).
5. If the HLSL fails to compile, repair it in one plan: set_module_enabled false on it and add_hlsl_module with a corrected copy under a new name.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: GPU with fixed bounds {{bounds}}, the stage and module present, 0 errors and 0 warnings, the emitter live, and the baseline and new particle counts.

presets.title: Give ambient effects one scalability budget
presets.summary: Create a Niagara effect type with update rate, distance and instance culls, assign it to the selected Systems and record the budget.

placeholders.name: update_frequency
placeholders.label: Update frequency
placeholders.hint: spawn_only, low, medium, high or continuous

presets.prompt:
Give the ambient effects {{selected_assets}} one scalability budget. Change only these Systems and the new effect type. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall `niagara scalability` for budgets the project already uses. hyper_niagara_inspect each System (load it with Epic's load_asset if needed) for its revision and the effect type it has now.
2. For the first System, one hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): create_effect_type at {{content_folder}}/{{effect_type}}.{{effect_type}}; set_effect_type_setting update_frequency {{update_frequency}}, cull_reaction {{cull_reaction}}, max_distance {{max_distance}} and max_instances {{max_instances}}; set_effect_type to it. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. For every other System, its own plan with only set_effect_type {{content_folder}}/{{effect_type}}.{{effect_type}} and a fresh operationId.
4. hyper_niagara_inspect with targetPath the effect type: its details show those settings. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready on each System, and inspect each: effectTypePath is the new type.
5. hyper_memory_remember the budget as a project convention, titled with its numbers.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table, one row per System (effect type assigned, 0 errors, 0 warnings), and one for the effect type's settings.

presets.title: Bake a golden sim cache to regression-test an effect
presets.summary: Make a CPU effect and its System deterministic, capture and bake its simulation as a golden cache, then prove a fresh capture matches it.
presets.prompt:
Lock down the effect {{selected_asset}} with a golden simulation cache so later edits can be regression-tested. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true and keep the revision. Sim capture takes CPU Systems only: if any emitter is GPUComputeSim, name it and stop.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): set_emitter_property determinism true and random_seed {{seed}} on each enabled emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId. A capture is deterministic only when the System is too: turn on its own Determinism (RandomSeed {{seed}}) with Epic's SetSystemData, save it, and inspect again.
3. hyper_niagara_validate with policy sim_cache_capture and captureFrames {{frames}}; call again with the returned captureId until its state is complete. framesCaptured must equal {{frames}} and bDeterministic be true.
4. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan with a fresh operationId and expectedRevision and one bake_sim_cache op: name = the captureId, assetPath {{content_folder}}/{{cache_name}}.{{cache_name}}.
5. Prove it: start a new sim_cache_capture with the same captureFrames, then poll it with its captureId plus goldenSimCachePath {{content_folder}}/{{cache_name}}.{{cache_name}} and floatTolerance 0.01 until complete: status matches_golden, bMatch true. hyper_niagara_inspect the cache path for its frames and emitters.
6. hyper_memory_remember that {{cache_name}} is the golden cache for this System and how it was made.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: determinism on (System and emitters), frames captured, cache baked at its path, the comparison matching (any differences listed).

presets.title: Create a Niagara Data Channel for bullet impacts
presets.summary: A data channel asset with typed impact variables, made beside the impact effect and verified by inspect, ready for gameplay to write hits.

placeholders.name: variables
placeholders.label: Variables (Name:type,...)
placeholders.hint: types: float, int32, bool, vector2, vector, vector4, position, linear_color, quat

presets.prompt:
Create a Niagara Data Channel for bullet impacts beside the impact effect {{selected_asset}}, so gameplay can write hits and one System can draw them all. Change nothing else. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_project_search (kinds asset, query `NDC_`) for data channels that already exist; reuse one that fits instead of adding a second. hyper_niagara_inspect {{selected_asset}} for its revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan on that System (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision) with a create_data_channel op: assetPath {{content_folder}}/{{channel_name}}.{{channel_name}}, valueType {{channel_type}}, value `{{variables}}`. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. hyper_niagara_inspect with targetPath the new channel: its details list exactly these variables with these types.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready on {{selected_asset}}: still 0 errors.
5. Say what remains by hand: a Data Channel reader in the System and the Blueprint write node, which these tools do not add.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: channel at its path, type {{channel_type}}, each variable present with its type, the System still clean.

presets.title: Make a team-coloured copy of an effect
presets.summary: Duplicate the selected effect, recolour every colour input to a team tint, keep it live, and prove the palette shift with captures.
presets.prompt:
Make a {{team}} copy of the effect {{selected_asset}}, tinted {{color}}, and leave the original untouched. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_niagara_inspect the original and note its revision. Duplicate it with Epic's duplicate into the same folder with the suffix `{{suffix}}`, and save the copy. hyper_niagara_inspect the copy with bIncludeTopology true: find every colour input per emitter (Initialize Particle, Color, Scale Color and the like).
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan on the copy (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): set_input_value with valueType color on each of those inputs (up to 96 ops), keeping each emitter's alpha and its brightness relative to the others. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. hyper_niagara_validate the copy with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe: the same emitters live as in the original.
4. Place the original and the copy in {{level}} 400 cm apart (leave the level unsaved). hyper_capture_view of each with source transform from the same offset (300 cm in front, looking at it), frameCount 1, warmupFrames 8.
5. Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: copy exists with the suffix, original unchanged (same revision as before), 0 errors and 0 warnings, all emitters live, the copy's frame shifted toward {{color}} (colorTemperatureK and meanSaturation compared). Show both frames on their own lines.

presets.title: Match an effect to a reference image
presets.summary: Capture the effect, score it against concept art with image compare in a session, and change one Niagara input per plan until the target.
presets.prompt:
Make the effect {{selected_asset}} look like the reference `{{reference}}`, following the image-match and unreal-niagara skills. Change only this System. If the niagara_vfx or lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. Open the reference and say in one sentence what makes its look: palette, shape, density, brightness. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true.
2. Place the System in {{level}} if it is not there and a CameraActor labelled `CAM_VFXMatch` (Epic's add_to_scene_from_class) framing it as the reference does; leave the level unsaved.
3. Baseline: hyper_capture_view (source camera, cameraActorLabel CAM_VFXMatch, frameCount 4, intervalSeconds 0.25), then hyper_image_compare with mode look, targetScore {{target}}, sessionId `vfx-match`, on the frame nearest the reference's moment.
4. At most {{max_iterations}} times: one hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, fresh expectedRevision) changing the one thing the compare ranks worst, with set_input_value (colour, size, spawn count, lifetime, velocity) or set_renderer_property. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId. Capture again and compare in the same session with a note. Keep a change only if the score rises; stop when it reaches {{target}} or stalls twice.
5. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: final score at least {{target}} (or the best and why it stopped), 0 errors, every emitter live; the score per iteration; the reference and the best frame each on its own line.

presets.title: Build GPU rain with splashes on the ground
presets.summary: Velocity-aligned rain streaks on the GPU over an area and short splashes at ground level, with bounded counts and captured frames.
presets.prompt:
Build rain `{{content_folder}}/NS_Rain`: `Rain` streaks falling about 900 cm/s over {{area}} x {{area}} cm, and `Splashes` at z 0. Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall `weather rain`. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): add_emitter `Rain` and `Splashes`, both from /Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/Fountain.Fountain; add_module /Niagara/Modules/Spawn/Location/BoxLocation.BoxLocation in each ParticleSpawnScript; set_emitter_property sim_target gpu and fixed_bounds covering the area up to 1300 cm on Rain; set_renderer_property Alignment VelocityAligned on Rain (rendererIndex 0); set_emitter_property `enabled` false on each template emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Inspect again (new revision, modules, inputs, renderer indexes), then one plan (up to 96 ops): set_module_enabled false on each ShapeLocation; set_input_value: Rain about {{rain_rate}} per second from a box at 1200 cm, 900 cm/s straight down, gravity 0, lifetime 1.3 s; Splashes from a flat box at z 0 over the area, small, rising 100-200 cm/s, 0.3 s.
4. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [Rain, Splashes].
5. Place it at the origin of {{level}} (unsaved); hyper_capture_view, source transform 800 cm away at eye height, frameCount 3, intervalSeconds 0.2.
6. Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: Rain on GPU with fixed bounds, both emitters live, Rain under {{rain_rate}} x 1.5, 0 errors and 0 warnings, frames differ. Show each frame on its own line as ![frame](path).

presets.title: Build a ribbon trail for a sword swing
presets.summary: A world-space ribbon on a continuous emitter, with width, fade time and tint set and its sprite renderer off, compiled and proven to spawn.
presets.prompt:
Build a sword swing trail `{{content_folder}}/{{system_name}}` to attach to a weapon socket: a `Trail` ribbon about {{width}} cm wide that fades over {{lifetime}} s, tinted {{color}}. Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): add_emitter `Trail` from /Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/Fountain.Fountain (it spawns continuously); add_renderer /Script/Niagara.NiagaraRibbonRendererProperties on Trail; set_renderer_property bIsEnabled false on its sprite renderer (rendererIndex 0); set_emitter_property local_space false, so the ribbon stays where the blade passed; set_emitter_property `enabled` false on each template emitter. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
3. Ribbons read Particles.RibbonWidth: add it with an add_set_parameters op (scriptName ParticleSpawnScript, name Particles.RibbonWidth, valueType float, value {{width}}) in the next plan.
4. One plan: set_module_enabled false on Trail's ShapeLocation, AddVelocity and GravityForce, so particles stay where they spawn; set_input_value for about 120 particles per second, lifetime {{lifetime}} and colour {{color}}; set_renderer_property FacingMode Screen and Shape Plane on the ribbon renderer (its rendererIndex from inspect).
5. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [Trail]; inspect lists a NiagaraRibbonRendererProperties renderer on Trail.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: ribbon renderer present, sprite renderer off, local space off, RibbonWidth {{width}} and lifetime {{lifetime}} as asked, 0 errors and 0 warnings, Trail live. Then say how to attach it: a Niagara component on the weapon's socket, activated for the swing window of the attack montage.

presets.title: Fill a room with drifting dust motes
presets.summary: Slow, tiny dust particles sized to the selected room's bounds, gently drifting on curl noise, capped by a budget and captured in place.
presets.prompt:
Fill the room around {{selected_actor}} with slow dust motes `{{content_folder}}/NS_DustMotes`, at most {{max_particles}} particles. Follow the unreal-niagara skill; if the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. Read the room's extent in cm with Epic's get_actor_bounds on {{selected_actor}}. Make an empty System with a hyper_niagara_apply_plan whose only op is create_system (targetPath the new System, expectedRevision empty, bDryRun false, a fresh operationId), then hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true; note the revision.
2. 3. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): set_renderer_property Material on each sprite renderer, /Game paths as object paths: M_FX_Glow for the glowing emitters, M_FX_Smoke for the smoke. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
4. hyper_niagara_inspect again for each renderer's Material; hyper_niagara_preview with the same ages; hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: both materials made at their paths, each renderer's Material set, 0 errors and 0 warnings, the after sheet with soft edges and smoke that is not a uniform grey. Show both sheets on their own lines.

presets.title: Animate smoke with a flipbook texture sheet
presets.summary: Make a flipbook smoke material, set the sprite renderer's grid and add a SubUV animation module so all three agree, then preview the frames.
presets.prompt:
Make `{{emitter}}` in {{selected_asset}} play the flipbook `{{texture}}` (a {{grid}} grid) over each particle's life. A flipbook needs three things to agree; follow the unreal-niagara skill's flipbook section. If the niagara_vfx or materials_dynamic_material pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true: `{{emitter}}`'s sprite renderer index, and whether a SubUVAnimation module is in its Particle Update; keep the revision. Confirm `{{texture}}` exists with Epic's AssetTools find_assets; if not, say so and stop.
2. hyper_material_recipe with Recipe particle_translucent, Path {{content_folder}}/M_FX_SmokeFlipbook, Settings texture {{texture}} and flipbook true: bDryRun true, then bDryRun false with a fresh OperationId; hyper_operation_wait if it waits for approval.
3. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision): set_renderer_property Material to the new material and SubImageSize {{grid}} on that renderer; add_module /Niagara/Modules/Update/SubUV/SubUVAnimation.SubUVAnimation in ParticleUpdateScript if it is missing. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
4. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeInputValues true: the module's inputs. If its frame range does not cover the {{grid}} grid, set it with set_input_value in one more plan, by the names inspect lists only.
5. hyper_niagara_preview with ages [0.3, 0.8, 1.5, 2.5] and background grey. Open it: puffs change shape from tile to tile instead of one image sliding. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready, then runtime_probe with expectEmitters [{{emitter}}].
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: the material samples the flipbook, SubImageSize {{grid}}, SubUVAnimation present, 0 errors and 0 warnings, the emitter live, the frames changing in the sheet. Show the sheet on its own line.

presets.title: Turn a looping effect into a one-shot burst
presets.summary: Set each emitter's loop behaviour to Once with an enum input, swap continuous spawning for a burst, and prove it lives then dies away.
presets.prompt:
Make {{selected_asset}} play once per activation: each emitter bursts {{count}} particles at the start and then stops, instead of looping. Change only this System. If the niagara_vfx pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeTopology true and bIncludeInputValues true: per emitter its EmitterState inputs (Loop Behavior), its SpawnRate module and any burst; keep the revision.
2. hyper_niagara_discover with kind modules and query "spawn burst" for the burst module's path, and kind script_schema on it for its input names.
3. One hyper_niagara_apply_plan (bDryRun false, fresh operationId, expectedRevision), per emitter: set_input_value on EmitterState's Loop Behavior with valueType enum and value Once; set_module_enabled false on SpawnRate; add_module the burst module in EmitterUpdateScript if it has none, and set_input_value its spawn count to {{count}} (int32). If a refusal lists the enum's entries, use the one it names for playing once. If the reply is queued, running or awaiting_user_approval, hyper_operation_wait with its operationId.
4. hyper_niagara_inspect with bIncludeInputValues true: `enum Once` on each emitter and SpawnRate off.
5. hyper_niagara_preview with ages [0.1, 0.5, 1.5, 4]: particles early, fewer later, none in the last tile if their lifetime is under 4 s.
6. hyper_niagara_validate with policy runtime_ready; runtime_probe with probeFrames 3; then probeFrames 600, which reports not_live by design once it has died away.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table per emitter: Loop Behavior Once, SpawnRate off, the burst count {{count}}, live at frame 3, zero at 10 s; 0 errors and 0 warnings. Show the sheet on its own line.
